**What issue #1 changed:** [Issue #1](https://github.com/sorincarbunaru/oxygen-batch-converter-addon-fork/issues/1) asked for a LaTeX to DITA conversion, and [commit 0ca6c10](https://github.com/sorincarbunaru/oxygen-batch-converter-addon-fork/commit/0ca6c1076f76f1eef9a6446f6def00133846de56) added it:

- **Pandoc location:** a new **Pandoc executable** field (with a **Browse** button) in the add-on's preferences page. If the field is empty, the converter uses the `pandoc` command on the `PATH`.
- **Split option:** a new **Create DITA maps from LaTeX documents containing multiple sections** option in the conversion dialog.
- **Menus:** the action appears in the Tools menu and in the DITA Maps Manager **Import** submenus.
- **Script:** the command-line script accepts `latex` or `tex` as the input format.
- **Behavior:** `\input` and `\include` resolve relative to each document's folder. Image links become absolute file URLs. Math stays as LaTeX source text. Pandoc has a 5-minute limit per document.

1. **`DITA/topics/batch-converter-addon.dita`**
   - Added "LaTeX to DITA (requires Pandoc)" to the list of conversions.
   - Added a **LaTeX to DITA** entry (`id="latexToDita"`) under Configuration. It covers Pandoc, the **Pandoc executable** preference, the split option and the behavior notes above.

2. **`DITA/topics/scripting_oxygen_batch_converter.dita`**
   - Added LaTeX to DITA to the list and `latex` (or `tex`) to the `-if` values.
   - Added a **LaTeX to DITA** section with the Pandoc requirement, how to point to Pandoc through the `-cs` settings file, and an example command.
3. **`DITA/topics/dita-migrating-various-formats.dita`**
   - The **Migrating LaTeX to DITA** section used to say: convert LaTeX to Word or HTML with Pandoc first, then convert that to DITA. It now points to the add-on's direct conversion and links to the new entry.
   - Fixed the "LaTex" spelling in the title and added a "LaTeX to DITA" index term.

**One thing to check:** I did not add LaTeX to the script's `-ss` (split sections) option. The commit links the split option to LaTeX for the AI tool, but I couldn't confirm that the script passes it on for LaTeX. Please ask the developer before adding it.

Manual Installation

To manually install the Batch Documents Converter add-on:

  1. Go to Help Install new add-ons to open an add-on selection dialog box.
  2. Enter or paste https://www.oxygenxml.com/InstData/Addons/default/updateSite.xml in the Show add-ons from field or select it from the drop-down menu.If you have issues connecting to the default update site, you can download the add-on package, unzip it, then use the Browse for local files action in the Install new add-ons dialog box to locate the downloaded addon.xml file.
  3. Select the Batch Documents Converter add-on and click Next.
  4. Read the end-user license agreement. Then select the I accept all terms of the end-user license agreement option and click Finish.
  5. Restart the application.

Result: A Batch Documents Converter submenu will now be available in the Tools menu and in the contextual menu. This submenu will contain a list of the various types of available conversions. Selecting one of the types of conversions will open a dialog box where you can configure options for the conversion.

Configuration

Options for configuring the conversions can be found in the preferences page of the add-on ( Options Preferences Plugins Batch Documents Converter ) or in the conversion dialog box.

Conversions from Word (Word Styles Mapping)

The conversions from MS Word work best if you only use the MS Word styles to semantically mark up your document. It is important that sections from the Word document are well defined using the heading styles.

Use the Word styles mapping option from the Batch Documents Converter preferences page to configure any of the types of Word conversions (Word to HTML, Word to DITA, Word to DocBook4, and Word to DocBook5) by setting a mapping between Word elements and styles to the corresponding HTML element.

If the Word document contains paragraphs formatted with custom styles that are not based on default styles, they have to be set in the Word styles mapping configuration. Those that are not set will be converted into simple paragraphs.

The styles mapping configuration is inherited between styles. If you use a custom style that is based on a default style, the default style mapping configuration will be inherited and also used for the custom style. The mapping from the base style is not inherited if the custom style has a mapping defined in the Word styles mapping configuration.

To define a mapping in the Word Styles Mapping table, you can use the already defined default configuration. For example, if you use a custom Word style named Document Title that is not based on a default style, you can map this to the HTML "h1" element:

Word element Word style HTML elements p Document Title h1:fresh

The resulting 'h1' element will be transformed into the corresponding element when converting to DITA, DocBook 4, and DocBook 5.

The Word styles mapping table contains the following columns:

Word element

This column allows one of the following Word elements:

  • p - Word paragraph
  • r - Word run
  • b - bold text
  • i - italicized text
  • u - underlined text
  • strike - strikethrough text
  • table - table
  • p:unorderd-list(x) - unordered list (where 'x' is the nesting level of the list)
  • p:orderd-list(x) - ordered list (where 'x' is the nesting level of the list)
Word style

This column can be used to map a paragraph, run, or table with a specific style (referenced by name).

Styles can also be referenced by style ID. This is the ID used internally in the .docx file. To map a paragraph or run with a specific style ID, append a dot followed by the style ID in the Word element column (for example: p.Heading1).
HTML elements

This column can be used to map the resulting HTML elements. It allows a single element or multiple nested elements.

The nested elements can be declared by using the '>' character (for example: ul > li).

The class attribute can be specified on the resulting HTML elements by appending a dot followed by the class value, after the element (for example: p.myClass).

When converting Word to DITA, these class attributes are automatically converted to outputclass attributes. This may be useful if you want to apply extra processing on the resulting DITA document using a custom XLS stylesheet.

The :fresh syntax can be used to create new elements. If it is not used, the converter will try to reuse the element and close it only when it is necessary.

For example, if the following configuration is set:

p Heading 1 h1

When the converter finds consecutive Word paragraphs with the style named Heading 1, these will be converted into a single h1 element that contains the text appended from all of the Word paragraphs.

If h1:fresh is set in the last column, the converter will create separate h1 elements.

The :separator('separator_string') syntax can be used to specify a separator between paragraphs that are merged when :fresh syntax is not specified.

For example, if the following configuration is set: p Code Block pre:separator('\n')

when the converter finds multiple consecutive paragraphs styled with the Code Block style, it will merge them into a single pre HTML element and the "\n" (new line) separator will be used between merged text.

To ignore elements, the '!' character can be added in the HTML elements column.

The Export button can be used to export the word styles configuration to an XML file. This exported file can be used to configure the MS Word Dynamic Conversiondynamic conversion from by copying the file in the DITA-OT plugin directory: [OXYGEN_INSTALL_DIR]/frameworks/dita/DITA-OT/plugins/com.oxygenxml.dynamic.resources.converter.

The Import button allows you to import the word styles configuration from an exported XML file.

The Word styles mapping configuration is applied only for the newer version of MS Word files formatted in the Microsoft Office Open XML (DOCX) format.

Maximum Heading Level for Creating Topics
The Maximum heading level for creating topics option from the Batch Documents Converter preferences page allows you to set a maximum heading level that the converter will process as DITA topics. The headings with a higher level will be converted to section elements.

When the output is a DITA topic, this option sets the maximum heading level that will be converted as a nested topic in the document.

When the output is a DITA map, this option sets the maximum heading level that will be extracted as a DITA topic file and referenced in the DITA map hierarchy.

This option only applies to the HTML to DITA, Word to DITA, and LaTeX to DITA conversions.
Word to DITA

The Create DITA maps from Word documents containing multiple headings option from the conversion dialog box allows you to decide whether the output will be a DITA map or a DITA topic. When this option is selected, the sections from your Word document marked by titles or headings will be separated into individual DITA topics and referenced in a DITA map. If the word document does not contain multiple sections, the output will be a single topic. When this option is not selected, the output will be a topic with nested topics and sections according to the number of titles and headings from the Word document. Mathematical equations in Word documents should be automatically converted to MathML equations if they are in Office Math Markup Language (OMML) format. If the mathematical equations are in Microsoft Equation Editor format, they first need to be converted to the newer OMML format. See: .
Markdown to DITA

The Create DITA maps from Markdown documents containing multiple headings option from the conversion dialog box allows you to decide whether the output will be a DITA map or a DITA topic. When this option is selected, all headings from your Markdown document will be separated into individual DITA topics and referenced in a DITA map. If the Markdown document does not contain multiple headings, the output will be a single topic. When this option is not selected, the output will be a topic with nested topics or sections according to the number of headings from the document.

The Create short description elements option from the conversion dialog box allows you to decide whether or not the shortdesc elements are created in the output DITA document. When this option is selected, the first paragraph before the headings from the Markdown document will be converted into DITA short description elements. When this option is not selected, the output will not contain the short description element.
HTML to DITA

The Create DITA maps from HTML documents containing multiple headings option from the conversion dialog box allows you to decide whether the output will be a DITA map or a DITA topic. When this option is selected, the headings from your HTML document will be separated into individual DITA topics and referenced in a DITA map. If the HTML document does not contain multiple sections, the output will be a single topic. When this option is not selected, the output will be a topic with nested topics or sections according to the number of headings from the document.

The Ignore HTML 'div' elements option from the conversion dialog box allows you to decide whether or not the div elements will be ignored. When this option is selected, all div elements will be ignored. When this option is not selected, only div elements that include the class or id attribute will be handled by the converter.

Confluence to DITA
The Confluence to DITA conversion processes the HTML content generated by the Atlassian Confluence (see ) export process. To export Confluence content to HTML, log in to your Atlassian Confluence account and navigate to the specific space that you want to export. Then go to Space Settings Export space and choose to export it as HTML. The resulting index.html file must be provided in the Input files list from the conversion dialog box.
DocBook to DITA
The Create DITA maps from DocBook documents containing multiple sections option from the conversion dialog box allows you to decide whether the output will be a DITA map or a DITA topic. When this option is selected, the sections from your DocBook document will be converted into individual DITA topics and referenced in a DITA map. When this option is not selected, the output will be a single topic with nested topics.
OpenAPI to DITA
The OpenAPI to DITA conversion can be used to convert JSON or YAML files that use and conform to the OpenAPI specification (versions 2.0, 3.0, or 3.1) into DITA documents. The Create DITA maps from OpenAPI documents option from the conversion dialog box allows you to decide whether the output will be a DITA map or a DITA topic. When this option is selected, the converter will create separate DITA topics for the introduction (including OAS 'Info', 'Server', 'Security Requirement' and 'External Documentation' objects), 'Tag', 'Operation', 'Callback', and 'Components' objects. These topics will be referenced in a DITA map. When this option is not selected, the output will be a single topic with nested topics.
LaTeX to DITA

The LaTeX to DITA conversion converts LaTeX documents (.tex, .latex, or .ltx) to DITA. It uses Pandoc to convert each LaTeX document to HTML, then converts the HTML to DITA. You must install Pandoc before you use this conversion.

By default, the converter runs the pandoc command found on the PATH. If Pandoc isn't on the PATH, set its location in the Pandoc executable field from the LaTeX to DITA section of the Batch Documents Converter preferences page. You can use the Browse button to select the file.

Use the Create DITA maps from LaTeX documents containing multiple sections option from the conversion dialog box to choose the output type. When you select this option, the converter creates a DITA topic for each section of your LaTeX document and references the topics in a DITA map. When you clear this option, the output is a single topic with nested topics or sections.

The following are some notes about the LaTeX to DITA conversion:

  • The converter resolves the LaTeX \input and \include commands relative to the folder of each document.
  • The converter writes image references as absolute file URLs, so that they resolve from the output folder.
  • The converter keeps math as LaTeX source text.
  • If Pandoc doesn't finish converting a document in 5 minutes, the conversion of that document fails.

Word to DITA Conversion Notes

The following are some notes about the Word to DITA conversion:

  • Paragraphs styled with default Word heading styles (or with custom styles based on default Word heading styles) are handled as topics or sections in the converted DITA output.
  • You can choose whether the converted output is a DITA map with referenced topics or a single DITA topic. See the Create DITA maps from Word documents containing multiple headings option.
  • You can choose the level of headings that are converted as topics or sections. See the option.
  • You can customize the conversion by adding mappings from your own Word styles to HTML elements. The configured HTML element is converted to the proper DITA element. The class attribute is transformed to the DITA outputclass attribute. See the section.
  • Ordered and unordered lists are converted to DITA and the list level is preserved.
  • Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, superscript, and subscript styles are converted to the corresponding DITA elements.
  • The formatting of table properties (such as borders) is currently ignored, but the formatting of the text inside the table is treated the same as in the rest of the document. Only the header row formatting is taken into account when converting tables to DITA.
  • Footnotes and endnotes are converted.
  • Images embedded in Word documents are saved to separate files and referenced in the generated DITA topics.
  • Links (cross-references and external links) are converted.
  • Line breaks and taken into account.
  • Mathematical equations in Word documents are automatically converted to MathML equations if they are in Office Math Markup Language (OMML) format. If the mathematical equations are in Microsoft Equation Editor format, they first need to be converted to the newer OMML format.
  • Symbols are converted.
  • Index entries are converted.
  • The Table of Contents is ignored in the DITA result.

When organizations decide to use DITA for structuring, developing, managing, or publishing content, they usually already have content written in other formats and need to convert it to DITA. There are a variety of possibilities for a conversion to DITA, depending on the original format of the content.

Migration from other formats to DITA is rarely perfect and manual changes may need to be made to the converted content, but the methods described below should help you find the best approach for your particular case.

Migrating Microsoft Office and Other Similar Types of Documents to DITA

There are various possibilities for migrating content from Microsoft Office® (and other Office-type formats) to DITA. For details, see .

Migrating DocBook Content to DITA

The Oxygen Batch Documents Converter add-on can be used for migrating one or multiple DocBook documents to DITA.

The provided DocBook to DITA conversion contains an option named Create DITA maps from DocBook documents containing multiple sections. When this option is selected, all sections from your DocBook document will be separated into individual DITA topics and referenced in a DITA map.

Migrating Google Docs to DITA

There are several possibilities to convert Google Docs to DITA:

  • Copy the content from Google Docs and paste it in an open DITA topic in Author mode. The Smart Paste functionality will attempt to convert the content to DITA.
  • Save the Google document as OpenDocumentFormat (ODF), then open it in the free LibreOffice application and save it as DocBook. Next, open the DocBook document in and run the built-in transformation scenario called DocBook to DITA.
  • If you want to convert multiple Google documents at once, save the documents as HTML, then use Oxygen's Batch Documents Converter add-on to convert the documents to DITA.

In all cases, you may need to make some manual adjustments in the resulting documents for elements that couldn't be mapped.

Migrating Markdown Content to DITA

There are several possibilities to convert Markdown content to DITA:

  • The DITA Open Toolkit publishing engine bundled with allows you to reference Markdown files directly in a DITA map and either publish them directly or export the Markdown files to DITA one by one. For details, see .
  • If you want to convert multiple Markdown files at once, you can use Oxygen's Batch Documents Converter add-on to convert the documents to DITA.

Migrating HTML Content to DITA

There are several possibilities to convert HTML content to DITA:

  • Copy the HTML content and paste it in an open DITA topic in Author mode. The Smart Paste functionality will attempt to convert the content to DITA.
  • Convert the HTML file to XHTML by selecting File Import/Convert HTML File to XHTML . Then, open the XHTML file and use one of the XHTML to DITA Transformation Scenarios to convert the content to DITA.
  • If you want to convert multiple HTML files at once, you can use Oxygen's Batch Converter add-on to convert the documents to DITA.
Migrating Unstructured FrameMaker to DITA

There is a blog post that details various possibilities for converting Unstructured FrameMaker content to DITA: Migrating Unstructured FrameMaker to DITA.

Migrating MadCap Content to DITA

This open-source project contains such a stylesheet that attempts to convert a Flare project to DITA XML along with instructions on how to use it. As an alternative, some recent MadCap versions seem to have facilities to export content directly to DITA.

Migrating Confluence to DITA

To migrate Confluence content to DITA, first export the content to HTML. For this, log in to your Confluence account and navigate to the specific space that you want to export. Then go to Space Settings Export space and choose to export it as HTML.

You can then use Oxygen's Batch Documents Converter add-on, selecting the Confluence to DITA action, to convert the exported index.html file into a DITA map with topics.

Migrating LaTeX to DITA

The Oxygen's Batch Documents Converter add-on provides a LaTeX to DITA conversion that you can use to convert one or more LaTeX documents to DITA. You must install Pandoc before you use this conversion. For details, see the LaTeX to DITA conversion options.

Migrating Other Formats to DITA

You may find third-party applications (such as Pandoc) that can convert your content to HTML or to some kind of XML format like DocBook. Once you have HTML or DocBook content, you can convert them to DITA using one of the methods described above.

Migrate from DITA to Confluence and Other Formats

There are various possible methods available for converting DITA content to Confluence and other formats (such as Microsoft Word or HTML). For details and ideas for some of the possible methods, see the DITA to Confluence blog post.

When organizations decide to use DITA for structuring, developing, managing, or publishing 20 content, they usually already have content written in other formats and need to convert it to 21 DITA. There are a variety of possibilities for a conversion to DITA, depending on the original 22 format of the content.

23

Migration from other formats to DITA is rarely perfect and manual changes may need to be made 24 to the converted content, but the methods described below should help you find the best 25 approach for your particular case.

26
27 Migrating Microsoft Office and Other Similar Types of Documents to DITA 28

There are various possibilities for migrating content from Microsoft Office® (and other 29 Office-type formats) to DITA. For details, see .

30
31
32 Migrating DocBook Content to DITA 33

The Oxygen Batch Documents Converter add-on 34 can be used for migrating one or multiple DocBook documents to DITA.

35

The provided DocBook to DITA conversion contains 36 an option named Create DITA maps from DocBook documents containing multiple sections. 37 When this option is selected, all sections from your DocBook document will be separated into 38 individual DITA topics and referenced in a DITA map.

39
40
41 Migrating Google Docs to DITA 42

There are several possibilities to convert Google Docs to DITA:

    43
  • Copy the content from Google Docs and paste it in an open DITA topic in 44 Author mode. The Smart Paste 46 functionality will attempt to convert the content to DITA.
    • 47
  • Save the Google document as OpenDocumentFormat (ODF), then open it in the free 48 LibreOffice application and save it as DocBook. Next, open the 49 DocBook document in and run the built-in transformation scenario 51 called DocBook to DITA.
    • 52
  • If you want to convert multiple Google documents at once, save 53 the documents as HTML, then use Oxygen's Batch Documents Converter add-on to convert 55 the documents to DITA.
    • 56

57

In all cases, you may need to make some manual adjustments in the resulting documents for 58 elements that couldn't be mapped.

59
60
61 Migrating Markdown Content to DITA 62

There are several possibilities to convert Markdown content to DITA:

    63
  • The DITA Open Toolkit publishing engine bundled with allows you 64 to reference Markdown files directly in a DITA map and either publish them directly or 65 export the Markdown files to DITA one by one. For details, see .
    • 67
  • If you want to convert multiple Markdown files at once, you can use Oxygen's Batch Documents Converter 69 add-on to convert the documents to DITA.
    • 70

73 Migrating HTML Content to DITA 74

There are several possibilities to convert HTML content to DITA:

75
    76
  • Copy the HTML content and paste it in an open DITA topic in 77 Author mode. The Smart Paste 79 functionality will attempt to convert the content to DITA.
    • 80
  • Convert the HTML file to XHTML by selecting 81 File 82 Import/Convert 83 HTML File to XHTML 84 . Then, open the XHTML file and use one of the XHTML to DITA Transformation Scenarios to convert the 87 content to DITA.
    • 88
  • If you want to convert multiple HTML files at once, you can use 89 Oxygen's Batch Converter 90 add-on to convert the documents to DITA.

94 Migrating Unstructured FrameMaker to DITA 95

There is a blog post that details various possibilities for converting 96 Unstructured FrameMaker content to DITA: Migrating Unstructured FrameMaker to DITA.

This open-source project contains such a stylesheet that attempts to 104 convert a Flare project to DITA XML along with instructions on how to use it. As an 105 alternative, some recent MadCap versions seem to have facilities to export content directly 106 to DITA.

To migrate Confluence content to DITA, first export the content to HTML. For this, log in 111 to your Confluence account and navigate to the specific space that you want to export. Then 112 go to 113 Space Settings 114 Export space 115 and choose to export it as HTML.

You may find third-party applications (such as Pandoc) that can convert your content to HTML or to 132 some kind of XML format like DocBook. Once you have HTML or DocBook content, you can convert 133 them to DITA using one of the methods described above.

Options for configuring the 122 conversions can be found in the preferences page of the add-on ( 123 Options 124 Preferences 125 Plugins 126 Batch Documents Converter 127 ) or in the conversion dialog box.

129

130 131
Conversions from Word (Word Styles Mapping)
132
133

The conversions from MS Word work best if you only use the MS Word styles to 134 semantically mark up your document. It is important that sections from the Word 135 document are well defined using the heading styles.

136

Use the Word styles mapping option from the Batch 137 Documents Converter preferences page to configure any of the types of 138 Word conversions (Word to HTML, Word to DITA, Word to DocBook4, and Word to 139 DocBook5) by setting a mapping between Word elements and styles to the corresponding 140 HTML element.

141

If the Word document contains paragraphs formatted with custom styles that are not 142 based on default styles, they have to be set in the Word styles mapping 143 configuration. Those that are not set will be converted into simple paragraphs.

144

The styles mapping configuration is inherited between styles. If you use a custom 145 style that is based on a default style, the default style mapping configuration will 146 be inherited and also used for the custom style. The mapping from the base style is 147 not inherited if the custom style has a mapping defined in the Word styles mapping 148 configuration.

149

To define a mapping in the Word Styles Mapping table, you 150 can use the already defined default configuration. For example, if you use a custom 151 Word style named Document Title that is not based on a default 152 style, you can map this to the HTML "h1" element:

153

154 155 156 Word element 157 Word style 158 HTML elements 159 160 161 p 162 Document Title 163 h1:fresh 164 165 166

167

The resulting 'h1' element will be transformed into the corresponding element when 168 converting to DITA, DocBook 4, and DocBook 5.

169

The Word styles mapping table contains the following 170 columns:

171

172

173 174
Word element
175
176

This column allows one of the following Word elements:

177
    178
  • p - Word paragraph
    • 179
  • r - Word run
    • 180
  • b - bold text
    • 181
  • i - italicized text
    • 182
  • u - underlined text
    • 183
  • strike - strikethrough text
    • 184
  • table - table
    • 185
  • p:unorderd-list(x) - unordered list (where 'x' is 186 the nesting level of the list)
    • 187
  • p:orderd-list(x) - ordered list (where 'x' is the 188 nesting level of the list)
    • 189
190
191 192 193
Word style
194

This column can be used to map a paragraph, run, or table with a specific 195 style (referenced by name).

Styles can also be referenced by style ID. 196 This is the ID used internally in the .docx file. To map a 197 paragraph or run with a specific style ID, append a dot followed by the style 198 ID in the Word element column (for example: 199 p.Heading1).
200 201 202
HTML elements
203
204

This column can be used to map the resulting HTML elements. It allows a 205 single element or multiple nested elements.

206

The nested elements can be declared by using the '>' character (for 207 example: ul > li).

208

The class attribute can be specified on the resulting HTML 209 elements by appending a dot followed by the class value, after the element 210 (for example: p.myClass).

211

When converting Word to DITA, these class attributes are 212 automatically converted to outputclass attributes. This may 213 be useful if you want to apply extra processing on the resulting DITA 214 document using a custom XLS stylesheet.

215

The :fresh syntax can be used to create new elements. If 216 it is not used, the converter will try to reuse the element and close it 217 only when it is necessary.

218

For example, if the following configuration is set:

219

220 221 222 p 223 Heading 1 224 h1 225 226 227

228

When the converter finds consecutive Word paragraphs with the style named 229 Heading 1, these will be converted into a single 230 h1 element that contains the text appended from all of 231 the Word paragraphs.

232

If h1:fresh is set in the last column, the converter will 233 create separate h1 elements.

234

The :separator('separator_string') syntax can be 235 used to specify a separator between paragraphs that are merged when 236 :fresh syntax is not specified.

237

For example, if the following configuration is set: 239 240 p 241 Code Block 242 pre:separator('\n') 243 244

245

when the converter finds multiple consecutive paragraphs styled with the 246 Code Block style, it will merge them into a single 247 pre HTML element and the "\n" (new line) 248 separator will be used between merged text.

249 250

To ignore elements, the '!' character can be added in the HTML 251 elements column.

252
253 254
255

256

The Export button can be used to export the word styles 257 configuration to an XML file. This exported file can be used to configure the MS 258 Word Dynamic Conversiondynamic conversion from by copying 261 the file in the DITA-OT plugin directory: 262 [OXYGEN_INSTALL_DIR]/frameworks/dita/DITA-OT/plugins/com.oxygenxml.dynamic.resources.converter.

263

The Import button allows you to import the word styles 264 configuration from an exported XML file.

265

266 The Word styles mapping 267 configuration is applied only for the newer version of MS Word files formatted in 268 the Microsoft Office Open XML (DOCX) format. 269

Maximum Heading Level for Creating Topics
274
The Maximum heading level for creating topics option from the 275 Batch Documents Converter preferences page allows you to set 276 a maximum heading level that the converter will process as DITA topics. The headings 277 with a higher level will be converted to section elements.

When 278 the output is a DITA topic, this option sets the maximum heading level that will be 279 converted as a nested topic in the document.

When the output is a DITA map, 280 this option sets the maximum heading level that will be extracted as a DITA topic 281 file and referenced in the DITA map hierarchy.

282
283 This option only applies to the HTML to DITA and Word to 284 DITA conversions. 285
286 287 288
Word to DITA
289
290

The Create DITA maps from Word documents containing multiple 291 headings option from the conversion dialog box allows you to decide 292 whether the output will be a DITA map or a DITA topic. When this option is selected, 293 the sections from your Word document marked by titles or headings will be separated 294 into individual DITA topics and referenced in a DITA map. If the word document does 295 not contain multiple sections, the output will be a single topic. When this option 296 is not selected, the output will be a topic with nested topics and sections 297 according to the number of titles and headings from the Word document. Mathematical equations in Word documents should be 299 automatically converted to MathML equations if they are in Office Math Markup 300 Language (OMML) format. If the mathematical equations are in Microsoft Equation 301 Editor format, they first need to be converted to the newer OMML format. See: 302 .

305

Markdown to DITA
309
310

The Create DITA maps from Markdown documents containing multiple 311 headings option from the conversion dialog box allows you to decide 312 whether the output will be a DITA map or a DITA topic. When this option is selected, 313 all headings from your Markdown document will be separated into individual DITA 314 topics and referenced in a DITA map. If the Markdown document does not contain 315 multiple headings, the output will be a single topic. When this option is not 316 selected, the output will be a topic with nested topics or sections according to the 317 number of headings from the document.

318

The Create short description elements option from the 319 conversion dialog box allows you to decide whether or not the 320 shortdesc elements are created in the output DITA document. When 321 this option is selected, the first paragraph before the headings from the Markdown 322 document will be converted into DITA short description elements. When this option is 323 not selected, the output will not contain the short description element.

324

HTML to DITA
328
329

The Create DITA maps from HTML documents containing multiple 330 headings option from the conversion dialog box allows you to decide 331 whether the output will be a DITA map or a DITA topic. When this option is selected, 332 the headings from your HTML document will be separated into individual DITA topics 333 and referenced in a DITA map. If the HTML document does not contain multiple 334 sections, the output will be a single topic. When this option is not selected, the 335 output will be a topic with nested topics or sections according to the number of 336 headings from the document.

337

The Ignore HTML 'div' elements option from the conversion 338 dialog box allows you to decide whether or not the div 339 elements will be ignored. When this option is selected, all 340 div elements will be ignored. When this option is not 341 selected, only div elements that include the 342 class or id attribute will be handled by the 343 converter.

344
345 346 347
Confluence to DITA
348
The Confluence to DITA conversion processes the HTML content 349 generated by the Atlassian Confluence (see ) export process. To export Confluence content to HTML, log in to your Atlassian Confluence account and navigate to the specific space 353 that you want to export. Then go to 354 Space Settings 355 Export space 356 and choose to export it as HTML. The resulting 357 index.html file must be provided in the Input 358 files list from the conversion dialog box.
359 360 361
DocBook to DITA
362
The Create DITA maps from DocBook documents containing multiple 363 sections option from the conversion dialog box allows you to decide 364 whether the output will be a DITA map or a DITA topic. When this option is selected, 365 the sections from your DocBook document will be converted into individual DITA topics 366 and referenced in a DITA map. When this option is not selected, the output will be a 367 single topic with nested topics.
368 369 370
OpenAPI to DITA
371
The OpenAPI to DITA conversion can be used to convert JSON or 372 YAML files that use and conform to the OpenAPI specification (versions 2.0, 3.0, or 373 3.1) into DITA documents. The Create DITA maps from OpenAPI 374 documents option from the conversion dialog box allows you to decide 375 whether the output will be a DITA map or a DITA topic. When this option is selected, 376 the converter will create separate DITA topics for the introduction (including OAS 377 'Info', 'Server', 'Security Requirement' and 'External Documentation' objects), 'Tag', 378 'Operation', 'Callback', and 'Components' objects. These topics will be referenced in 379 a DITA map. When this option is not selected, the output will be a single topic with 380 nested topics.
381 382
383

384
385
386 Word to DITA Conversion Notes 387

The following are some notes about the Word to DITA conversion:

    389
  • Paragraphs styled with default Word heading styles (or with custom 390 styles based on default Word heading styles) are handled as topics or sections in the 391 converted DITA output.
    • 392
  • You can choose whether the converted output is a DITA map with 393 referenced topics or a single DITA topic. See the Create DITA maps from Word 395 documents containing multiple headings option.
    • 396
  • You can choose the level of headings that are converted as topics 397 or sections. See the option.
    • 399
  • You can customize the conversion by adding mappings from your own 400 Word styles to HTML elements. The configured HTML element is converted to the proper 401 DITA element. The class attribute is transformed to the DITA 402 outputclass attribute. See the section.
    • 404
  • Ordered and unordered lists are converted to DITA and the list 405 level is preserved.
    • 406
  • Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, superscript, and subscript 407 styles are converted to the corresponding DITA elements.
    • 408
  • The formatting of table properties (such as borders) is currently 409 ignored, but the formatting of the text inside the table is treated the same as in the 410 rest of the document. Only the header row formatting is taken into account when 411 converting tables to DITA.
    • 412
  • Footnotes and endnotes are converted.
    • 413
  • Images embedded in Word documents are saved to separate files and 414 referenced in the generated DITA topics.
    • 415
  • Links (cross-references and external links) are converted.
    • 416
  • Line breaks and taken into account.
    • 417
  • Mathematical equations in Word documents are automatically 418 converted to MathML equations if they are in Office Math Markup Language (OMML) 419 format. If the mathematical equations are in Microsoft Equation Editor format, 420 they first need to be converted to the newer OMML format.
    • 421
  • Symbols are converted.
    • 422
  • Index entries are converted.
    • 423
  • The Table of Contents is ignored in the DITA result.
    • 424

## Purpose

Use this skill to turn a GitHub issue from the Batch Documents Converter project into a documentation update and a pull request for the user guide.

## What You Need

1. **The issue number.** If the user does not give one, ask for it.

   - Use `search_project_resources` or `grep_project` to find other related topics (for example, `dita-migrating-various-formats.dita` for new conversions to DITA).
4. **Access to GitHub tools** to create a branch, push files, and create the pull request.

## Workflow

1. **Read the issue.** Find out what changed in the converter (for example, a new conversion type, a new option, or a changed behavior).
2. **Find the affected topics.** Check how the existing documentation describes the feature. Follow the same structure and wording.

Run `validate_content` and `term_check_document_content` on each changed topic, and fix the problems found. 6. **Create the pull request** with `github_create_pull_request`:
   - `owner`: `sorincarbunaru`, `repo`: `userguide-public`.
   - `base`: `master`, `head`: the new branch.
   - Title: a short summary of the docs change.
   - Body: a summary of the changes, the list of changed topics, and a link to the source issue (`https://github.com/sorincarbunaru/oxygen-batch-converter-addon-fork/issues/<number>`).
7. **Report** the pull request link and the list of changed topics to the user. Recommend a human review of the changes.
